svg.title: 1212 Lobdel Avenue — Corrected E-W Orientation Options A and C with 20ft front / 15ft rear setbacks
svg.desc: Two corrected site plans for E-W oriented lot configurations. Option A: 2 N-S rows, 10 units each, 20 units total, clean code. Option C: 2 N-S rows, 16 units each with fire wall, 32 units total. Both show 20ft front setback from private aisle, 35ft building, 15ft rear yard, with back-to-back rear yards forming a 30ft combined zone. All four options compared in summary table.

path.aria-label: E-W Orientation — Corrected Setbacks: 20 ft front / 15 ft rear
E-W orientation · 2 back-to-back N-S rows · no fire wall · 20ft front / 15ft rear
South entry cross-drive · 20 ft (from Lobdel Ave)
E-W orientation · 2 N-S rows · 8+8 fire wall · 20ft front / 15ft rear
Argument for 15 ft rear yard variance (R-3 standard: 20 ft)
1. Combined rear zone = 15 + 15 = 30 ft — exceeds the 20 ft standard
by 10 ft. The code intent (light, air, privacy) is fully met.
2. Rear does NOT abut a public street — 20 ft standard was designed
for rear lots abutting alleys/streets, not back-to-back private yards.
3. Historic Wilmington rowhouses: 0–5 ft rear yards are standard.
A 15 ft rear is generous by Wilmington's built context.
4. 15 ft rear programmed as bio-swale / rain garden strip — higher-value
green infrastructure than an unprogrammed 20 ft grass yard.
5. WHA affordable homeownership project — public benefit supports
minor variance enabling +4 to +12 additional affordable units.
Q1. Does the private N-S drive aisle constitute a "street" for front
setback purposes under Chapter 48? (Determines front setback direction)
Q2. For E-W oriented lots, does a 20 ft setback from Lobdel Ave
still apply as a side or other setback?
Q3. Will the Zoning Administrator grant a 15 ft rear yard where
combined back-to-back rears = 30 ft, or is a ZBA variance needed?
Q4. Can the 30 ft combined rear zone be designated as a shared
green infrastructure easement (bio-swale) on the recorded plat?
Q5. Does the private drive easement satisfy R-3 access requirements
for fee-simple lots without public street frontage?
A — E-W, 2 rows, no fire wall
B — N-S orient., full indep. setbacks
15 ft rear variance + fire wall + pre-app
Easement plat + city rear yard confirm.
E-W orientation design notes (Options A and C):
Units face east or west — primary entry from perimeter drive loop or cross-drives at S end. No units face Lobdel Ave directly.
Back-to-back configuration: Row W units face west (toward W perimeter drive), Row E units face east (toward E perimeter/buffer).
30 ft combined rear zone between the two rows is the critical variance argument — programs as bio-swale, rain garden, or shared garden strip.
Option C fire wall at unit 8/9 in both rows — rated assembly, direct application for AAC autoclaved aerated concrete party wall panel (Merge4Ward campus).
All E-W yields are contingent on pre-application meeting confirmation. Option D remains the strongest yield without variance risk.
Parcel 2605130241 · 175 ft × 352.6 ft · 1.39 ac · R-3, Chapter 48, City of Wilmington
